question: In the US, which germ causes the most food poisoning: Salmonella, Listeria, Campylobacter or norovirus?
answer: Norovirus, about 5.5 million of the 9.4 million US cases traced to a known germ each year, Scallan's CDC team estimated. It usually travels on hands rather than in raw meat: a sick cook, a shared bowl. Alcohol gel works poorly against it; the CDC advises washing hands with soap and water.
move: Find out how a germ travels before deciding how to clean.
source: Scallan et al., Emerging Infectious Diseases, 2011
reference: Scallan, E. et al. (2011) Foodborne illness acquired in the United States: major pathogens, Emerging Infectious Diseases 17(1): 7-15; CDC, Preventing Norovirus
ask: Before I handle food, do I wash my hands with soap or reach for gel?

items.label: Salmonella
items.note: A fifth as many cases as norovirus, but it kills more Americans.

items.label: Listeria
items.note: Rare, about 1,600 cases, but about 1 in 6 of them dies.

items.label: Norovirus
items.note: Over half of all cases, often from food handled by someone already ill.
